s: 本セミナーは、当社の会員（　　）、関心のある方ならどなたでもご参加いただけます。
en: This seminar is not just for our members: anyone who is interested is welcome to attend.
why: 〜に限らず: not limited to X, a wider range is included too. Members first, then anyone at all (どなたでも).
〜に限り means 'only X', as a special exception. 'Members only' clashes with 'anyone who is interested'.
〜に限って picks out one case as unusual or unlucky ('of all times'). It cannot open the door to everyone.
〜にかけては names a skill where someone is the best. 会員 is not a skill, and nothing here is praise.
tell: X, then a wider-range word (どなたでも・いつも・みんな): に限らず, not に限り.

s: A「駅前のカフェ、週末はいつも混んでるね。」B「週末（　　）、平日もけっこう混んでるんだよ。」
en: A: The cafe by the station is always packed at weekends. B: Not just at weekends. It's pretty busy on weekdays too.
why: 〜に限らず: not limited to X. 平日も adds a wider range beyond weekends, and it is fine in casual speech.
〜に限って makes weekends the one special case. 平日も says weekdays are busy too, so the sentence contradicts itself.
〜に限り means 'only X'. 'Only at weekends' clashes with 平日も.
〜からして judges the whole from one small detail, usually as criticism. Weekends are not a detail, and 平日も widens the range instead.
tell: X, then a wider range with も (平日も・みんな): に限らず. に限り and に限って narrow it to X.

s: この問題はこれまで都市部だけのものだと考えられてきたが、実は都市部（　　）ことが、今回の調査で明らかになった。
en: This problem had long been thought to affect only cities, but the survey showed that it is in fact not limited to them: it is happening in rural areas too.
c: に限らず、地方でも起きている
に限って、地方でも起きている
に限らず、地方では起きていない
に限り、地方でも起きている
why: 〜に限らず opens the range beyond X, so the second half adds more places with も: 地方でも起きている.
〜に限って singles out X as the special or unlucky case. It cannot then add 地方でも.
After 〜に限らず the wider range must be included. 地方では起きていない takes it away again, so the sentence contradicts itself.
〜に限り means 'only in X', as on a notice. 'Only in cities' clashes with 'in rural areas too'.
cue: だけのものだと考えられてきた
tell: After に限らず the wider range must be included (〜も・〜でも). A negative after it contradicts.

s: 新しい制度は、手続きを簡単にした（　　）、利用者の費用の負担も大きく減らした。
en: The new system not only simplified the procedures but also greatly reduced the cost burden on users.
why: 〜のみならず attaches to a plain-form clause (簡単にした) as well as a noun. Formal 'not only… but also', with 〜も after.
〜に限らず attaches only to a noun. It cannot follow a verb like 簡単にした.
〜はもとより attaches only to a noun (or a noun plus a particle). 簡単にしたはもとより is broken.
〜をはじめ also needs a noun: the first example of a group (東京をはじめ). It cannot follow a verb.
tell: A verb clause before the blank rules out に限らず, はもとより, をはじめ (noun only). のみならず takes clauses.

s: 地球温暖化は、環境の問題（　　）、食料や経済にも深刻な影響を及ぼす社会全体の課題である。
en: Global warming is not only an environmental problem: it is an issue for the whole of society, with serious effects on food and the economy as well.
why: 〜のみならず is the formal 'not only', and a noun joins it through である. It matches the written ending 課題である.
〜のに対して contrasts two different things (A is X, whereas B is Y). Here one subject gets two points that add up (〜にも).
〜ばかりに means 'simply because of X, something bad happened'. There is no cause and bad result here.
〜上で means 'after doing X' or 'in doing X'. It does not add a second point.
tell: Formal essay (〜である) + 'not only… but also' (〜にも): noun + であるのみならず.

s: 彼は無断で仕事を休んだ（　　）、連絡すら取ろうとしなかった。
en: Not only did he skip work without telling anyone, he didn't even try to get in touch.
why: 〜ばかりか: X is already bad, and something even worse is piled on top, often with すら・さえ・まで.
〜上で means 'after doing X carefully, then the next step'. Skipping work is not a first step toward anything.
〜次第 (as soon as) attaches to the ます stem (休み次第) and must lead into a plan or request. Neither fits here.
〜からして attaches to a noun and means 'judging even from X'. It cannot follow a verb like 休んだ.
tell: Bad, then even worse with すら・さえ・まで: ばかりか.

s: A「先月入った中村さん、どう？」B「すごいよ。仕事が早い（　　）、先輩のミスまで見つけてくれるんだ。」
en: A: How's Nakamura, who joined last month? B: Amazing. Not only is she fast, she even catches her seniors' mistakes.
why: 〜ばかりか: X is already impressive, then something even more surprising (まで). It works in everyday speech.
〜ばかりに means 'just because of X, something bad happened'. Nothing bad happens here.
〜ばかりで means 'only X and nothing else', usually a complaint. It clashes with the praise that follows.
〜はもとより attaches to a noun (仕事はもとより). It cannot follow the adjective 早い directly.
tell: A surprise on top of a surprise (まで) in casual speech: ばかりか. Not ばかりに (bad result) or ばかりで (only).

s: この掃除機は音が静かなばかりか、（　　）。
en: Not only is this vacuum cleaner quiet, its electricity costs are also amazingly low.
c: 電気代も驚くほど安い
ぜひ一度お試しください
吸い込む力はやや弱い
音が静かなのが特徴だ
why: After 〜ばかりか comes a second point in the same direction that is even more notable, often with も or まで.
〜ばかりか cannot be followed by a request or invitation. お試しください is a request.
やや弱い is a minus point. 〜ばかりか adds something in the same direction, not a drawback.
This only repeats the first point. 〜ばかりか needs a new and bigger point.
tell: After ばかりか: a bigger point in the same direction (〜も・〜まで). No request, no drawback.

s: この祭りは、地元の住民に（　　）、海外からの旅行者にも広く知られている。
en: This festival is well known to local residents, of course, and to travellers from abroad as well.
why: 〜はもとより can follow a noun plus a particle (住民にはもとより). The first group is obvious, and 〜にも adds another.
〜に限らず attaches straight to a noun. After the particle に it breaks: 住民にに限らず.
〜をはじめ also attaches straight to a noun, so 住民にをはじめ is broken.
〜上に needs a plain form or 名の, and it stacks qualities of one thing. It cannot follow the particle に or list groups of people.
tell: Noun + particle + blank, then 〜にも: only はもとより can follow a particle.

s: 台風の接近に備え、水や食料（　　）、懐中電灯や携帯ラジオなども早めに準備しておいてください。
en: With the typhoon approaching, please get ready early: water and food, of course, but also torches, portable radios and so on.
why: 〜はもとより: X goes without saying (water and food), and 〜も adds more. A request may follow it.
〜ばかりか cannot be followed by a request (〜てください). It also needs a surprising step up, not a checklist.
〜に限り means 'only X'. It clashes with なども, which adds more items.
〜にかけては names a skill where someone is the best. Water and food are not skills.
cue: 準備しておいてください
tell: Obvious item + 〜も + a request (〜てください): はもとより. ばかりか cannot take a request.

s: このパソコンは性能が優れている（　　）、デザインも洗練されていて使いやすい。
en: This computer performs superbly, and on top of that its design is refined and easy to use.
why: 〜上に stacks two points with the same evaluation: good performance, plus good design (〜も).
〜上で means 'after doing X, then Y', a sequence. Performance and design are not steps.
〜反面 sets a plus against a minus. Both halves here are plus points.
〜ばかりで means 'only X and nothing else', a complaint. It clashes with デザインも.
tell: Plus + plus (or minus + minus) with 〜も: 上に. 上で is a sequence, 反面 a contrast.

s: この部屋は駅から遠い（　　）、日当たりも悪いので、家賃が安いのも当然だ。
en: This flat is far from the station and gets little sun on top of that, so no wonder the rent is cheap.
why: 〜上に stacks two minus points (far away, little sun). Same evaluation on both sides, joined by 〜も.
〜上で means 'after doing X'. 遠い is a state, not a step you take first.
〜反面 contrasts a plus with a minus. Here both points are minuses.
〜わりに means 'considering X, surprisingly Y'. Little sun is not a surprise given that the flat is far away.
tell: Minus + minus (〜も): 上に. Check that both halves point the same way.

s: この店の料理はおいしい上に、（　　）。
en: The food at this restaurant is delicious, and the prices are reasonable too.
c: 店員の態度はいまひとつだ
ぜひ一度行ってみてください
why: 〜上に needs a second point with the same evaluation. Tasty food (plus) and fair prices (plus) match.
So-so service is a minus. 〜上に never joins a plus to a minus.
〜上に cannot be followed by a request or invitation (〜てください).
Being far from the station is a minus, so it does not stack with the plus of tasty food.
tell: After 上に: another point with the same evaluation, often with 〜も. No request, no opposite.

s: 新製品の安全性（　　）ご質問は、お客様相談窓口までお寄せください。
en: Please send any questions about the safety of the new product to our customer help desk.
why: 〜に関する + noun: about a broad theme. Questions about safety ask for information, which is what に関する is for.
〜にこたえる only takes expectations or requests (期待・要望). 安全性 is neither.
〜向けの means 'made for a target group'. 安全性 is not a group of people.
〜に沿った means 'in line with a plan or policy'. A question does not follow safety like a plan.
tell: A theme + information words (質問・調査・資料): に関する.

s: 今回のシステム障害の原因（　　）、社内の調査チームが詳しく調べている。
en: An internal investigation team is looking closely into the cause of the recent system failure.
why: 〜に関して: about a broad theme, followed by an information verb (調べる・調査する・説明する).
〜にかけては praises a skill where someone is the best. A cause is not a skill.
〜に対して aims an action or feeling at a target (a person, a question). You do not 'investigate toward' a cause.
〜に応じて means 'adjusting to something that varies'. Nothing is being adjusted here.
tell: A topic + an information verb (調べる・調査する・説明する): に関して.

s: 来月の研修の日程（　　）、決まり次第、改めてご連絡いたします。
en: As for the schedule for next month's training, we will contact you again as soon as it is decided.
why: 〜に関しましては is the polite form of に関しては: 'as for X', used in business emails to raise a topic.
〜をめぐって is for a dispute between several sides. Nobody is fighting over a training schedule.
〜にかけては praises a skill where someone is unbeatable. A schedule is not a skill.
〜にこたえて responds to an expectation or request (期待・要望). 日程 is neither.
tell: A business email raising a topic: 〜に関しましては (polite に関しては).

s: 新工場の建設予定地（　　）、住民と市の間で対立が続いている。
en: Residents and the city remain in conflict over the planned site for the new factory.
why: 〜をめぐって: several parties disagree over X. 住民と市 and 対立 show the dispute.
〜に対して aims an action or attitude at one target. A conflict between two sides is not aimed at the site.
〜にかけては praises a skill where someone is the best. A building site is not a skill.
〜にこたえて means 'living up to an expectation or request'. A building site is neither.
tell: Two or more sides + 対立・議論・争い: をめぐって.

s: 最後の一議席（　　）、三人の候補者が激しく争った。
en: Three candidates fought fiercely over the last remaining seat.
why: 〜をめぐって: several people compete or argue over X. 三人の候補者 and 争った mark the contest.
〜にかけては praises someone's skill where nobody beats them. A seat in parliament is not a skill.
〜にこたえて means living up to an expectation or request. 議席 is neither.
〜に沿って means following a plan, policy or route. Candidates do not follow a seat; they fight over it.
tell: The prize several people fight over (議席・遺産・優勝) + 争う: をめぐって.

s: 微妙な味の違いを見分けること（　　）、この店の料理長の右に出る者はいない。
en: When it comes to telling subtle differences in flavour, nobody beats this restaurant's head chef.
why: 〜にかけては: a skill, then 'nobody is better' (右に出る者はいない). It is always praise.
〜をめぐって is for a dispute between several sides. Nobody is arguing here.
〜に対して aims an action or feeling at a target. 右に出る者はいない is not aimed at anything.
〜にこたえて responds to an expectation or request. A tasting skill is neither.
tell: A skill + 右に出る者はいない・誰にも負けない: にかけては.

s: うちの兄は、料理の腕にかけては（　　）。
en: When it comes to cooking, my older brother is confident he can match any professional.
c: プロにも負けないと自信を持っている
まだまだ練習が必要だ
あまり興味がないらしい
毎週料理教室に通っている
why: 〜にかけては must lead to 'nobody beats them' or 'the best'. プロにも負けない is exactly that praise.
〜にかけては is always praise. Saying he still needs practice is criticism, so it cannot follow.
Having little interest says nothing about being the best. 〜にかけては needs a top-level judgement.
Going to a cooking class is just a habit. 〜にかけては needs 'nobody is better', not a plain fact.
tell: After にかけては comes top praise (誰にも負けない・一番だ). Criticism or plain facts do not fit.

s: 新入社員の中には、取引先の人（　　）友達のような話し方をする人もいて、困っている。
en: Some of our new employees talk to people from client companies as if they were friends, which is a problem.
why: 〜に対して aims an action or attitude at a person: the way you speak to clients.
〜に関して introduces a topic to research or explain. Speaking to someone is not discussing a topic.
〜をめぐって is for several sides arguing over X. Nobody is arguing over the clients.
〜にかけては praises a skill. 取引先の人 is not a skill, and this is a criticism.
tell: An action or way of speaking aimed at a person: に対して.

s: 部下（　　）厳しすぎる態度は、かえってやる気を失わせることがある。
en: Being too harsh toward your staff can end up killing their motivation.
why: 〜に対する + noun: an attitude aimed at a person. 部下に対する態度 is 'your attitude toward your staff'.
〜に関する + noun means 'about a theme' (資料・調査). An attitude is not information about staff.
〜をめぐる + noun is for a dispute (争い・議論) among several sides. 態度 is not a dispute.
〜向けの + noun means 'made for a target group', like a product or a book. An attitude is not a product.
tell: 態度・気持ち・反応 aimed at someone: に対する. に関する is for information.

s: 兄が社交的で友人が多い（　　）、弟は物静かで、一人で本を読むのが好きだ。
en: Whereas the older brother is sociable and has lots of friends, the younger one is quiet and likes reading on his own.
why: Clause + の + に対して: 'whereas'. Two people (兄が, 弟は) are set against each other with a clear difference.
Without の, に対して means 'toward' and needs a noun. It cannot follow the clause 多い.
〜ばかりか adds a bigger point in the same direction. Here the second half is the opposite of the first, about a different person.
〜上に stacks two points about the same subject with the same evaluation. It does not contrast two people.
tell: Two subjects (Aが…、Bは…) with a clear difference: clause + のに対して.

s: この会社では、男性社員の育児休業の取得率が三割程度（　　）、女性社員はほぼ全員が取得している。
en: At this company, only about 30% of male employees take childcare leave, whereas almost all female employees do.
why: Noun + である + の + に対して: 'whereas'. Men (about 30%) and women (almost all) are clearly contrasted.
The の is missing. Without it, に対して means 'toward' and cannot follow である.
に対する must be followed by a noun (〜に対する意見). Here a clause follows, so it must be に対して.
〜にしても means 'even if X'. The sentence does not concede anything; it compares two groups.
tell: Two groups compared in a report: Xであるのに対して、Yは… Keep the の, and use て before a clause.

s: 地元ファンの大きな期待（　　）、選手たちは最後まで走り続け、見事な逆転勝利を収めた。
en: Living up to the high hopes of their home fans, the players kept running to the end and pulled off a superb come-from-behind win.
why: 〜にこたえて: act so as to live up to someone's hopes, cheers or requests (期待・声援・要望).
〜に応じて adjusts to something that varies (予算・体力) or accepts a request. 期待 does not take 応じる; you live up to it with こたえる.
〜をめぐって is for a dispute between several sides. Nobody is arguing about the fans' hopes.
〜に対して aims an action straight at a target. Winning the game is not aimed at the fans' hopes.
tell: 期待・声援・要望 + an action that lives up to it: にこたえて. 期待に応じる is not said.

s: お客様からの多くのご要望に（　　）、来月より営業時間を夜十時まで延長することにいたしました。
en: In response to many requests from our customers, we have decided to extend our opening hours to 10 p.m. from next month.
why: ご要望にこたえて, in humble form: お応えする. The shop is the one responding, so the humble form matches いたしました.
お〜になる is honorific. It raises the subject, but the subject is the shop itself. Never use honorifics for your own action.
応えられて reads as honorific, passive or potential. None of these is the shop's own humble action.
〜てくださる means someone else does something for us. The shop is responding, not the customers.
tell: Our own response to customers' requests: ご要望にお応えして + a humble ending (いたしました).

s: この映画は、実際に起きた事件（　　）作られたフィクションである。
en: This film is a work of fiction based on a real incident.
why: 〜をもとにして: use X as source material to create something new. 作られた is the creation verb.
〜にこたえて means living up to an expectation or request (期待・要望). An incident is neither.
〜のもとで means 'under a person' (先生のもとで). An incident is not a person you work under.
〜向けに means 'made for a target group'. An incident is not an audience.
tell: Source material + a creation verb (作る・書く・デザインする): をもとにして.

s: その作家は、祖父が戦時中に家族へ送った手紙（　　）、一編の小説を書き上げた。
en: The writer produced a novel based on the letters his grandfather sent to the family during the war.
why: 〜をもとに: the letters are source material for something new, a novel (書き上げた).
〜のもとで means 'under a person's guidance' (先生のもとで). Letters are not a person.
〜のもとに means 'under a condition' (管理・了解・名). Letters are not a condition you act under.
〜向けに means 'made for a target group'. Letters are not an audience.
tell: を + もと = source material for creating. の + もと = under a person or a condition.

s: この絵本の物語は、作者が子どものころに祖母から聞いた昔話（　　）。
en: Apparently, the story in this picture book is based on a folk tale the author heard from their grandmother as a child.
c: をもとにしているそうだ
のもとにしているそうだ
に基づかれているそうだ
をもとにさせているそうだ
why: 〜をもとにしている: the folk tale is the source the story was built from. そうだ adds 'I hear'.
のもとに means 'under a condition' and never takes する. のもとにしている is broken.
基づく is intransitive, so it has no passive. The correct shape would be に基づいている.
〜させる (causative) means 'make someone do it'. Nobody is being made to do anything here.
tell: A story built from source material: 〜をもとにしている. Watch for fake passives and causatives.

s: この国では、法律（　　）、飲酒運転をした者は厳しく罰せられる。
en: In this country, anyone who drives drunk is severely punished in accordance with the law.
why: 〜に基づいて: act or judge by a fixed criterion. A law is the classic criterion for punishing someone.
〜にこたえて means living up to an expectation or request (期待・要望). A law is neither.
〜に応じて means 'adjusting to something that varies' (予算・年齢). The law is not a variable.
〜向けに means 'made for a target group'. The law is not an audience.
tell: A rule or law + judge, punish or decide: に基づいて.

s: 委員会は、アンケートの結果（　　）、来年度の予算の配分を決定した。
en: The committee decided how to allocate next year's budget on the basis of the survey results.
why: 〜に基づいて: use X as the criterion for a decision. 決定する is the deciding verb.
〜向けに means 'made for a target group'. Survey results are not an audience.
〜のもとで means 'under a person or a principle' (先生のもとで). Results are not someone you work under.
〜にこたえて responds to an expectation or request (要望にこたえて). Results do not ask for anything.
tell: Evidence as the yardstick for a judgement (判断する・決定する): に基づいて.

s: 本規則第五条（　　）、以下に該当する方の入場をお断りいたします。
en: In accordance with Article 5 of these rules, we will refuse entry to anyone who falls under the following.
why: 〜に基づき is the formal written form of に基づいて. The rule is the criterion for refusing entry.
〜向けに means 'made for a target group'. An article of the rules is not an audience.
〜に応じ means adjusting to something that varies (人数・年齢に応じ). An article of the rules does not vary.
〜にこたえ means living up to an expectation or request (要望にこたえ). An article of the rules is neither.
tell: A rule or article + an official decision on a notice: 〜に基づき.

s: 業務の混乱を防ぐため、作業は必ず安全マニュアル（　　）進めてください。
en: To avoid confusion, always carry out the work in line with the safety manual.
why: 〜に沿って: follow a manual, plan or policy step by step without straying. 進める is the flow of work.
〜向けに means 'made for a target group'. A manual is not an audience.
〜をめぐって is for a dispute. Nobody is arguing over the manual.
〜にこたえて responds to an expectation or request. A manual is neither.
tell: A manual, plan or policy + carrying on step by step (進める): に沿って.

s: このマラソン大会のコースは川（　　）作られていて、走りながら両岸の桜を楽しむことができる。
en: The course of this marathon runs along the river, so runners can enjoy the cherry blossoms on both banks.
why: 〜に沿って also means 'along' something long: a river, a road, a coast. The course follows the river.
〜をもとに is for source material you create from. A river is not material for a course.
〜に基づいて is for a criterion you judge by (法律・データ). A river is not a criterion.
〜のもとで means 'under a person'. A river is not a person.
tell: Something long you follow (川・道・方針・マニュアル): に沿って.

s: お客様のご希望に（　　）、スタッフ一同、心を込めてお手伝いいたします。
en: All of our staff will do our very best to help, so that we can meet your wishes.
why: ご希望に沿う = meet the customer's wishes. 沿える (can meet) + よう (so that) states the staff's own aim.
沿われる would be honorific or passive. Staff never raise their own action with honorifics.
お〜になる is honorific. It cannot describe the staff's own action.
〜てもらう means someone else does it for you. The staff are the ones who must meet the wishes.
tell: Our promise to customers: ご希望・ご期待に沿えるよう + a humble ending.

s: 厳しい指導で知られる名監督（　　）、選手たちは毎日の練習に励んでいる。
en: Under a famous coach known for his strict training, the players work hard at practice every day.
why: Person + のもとで: under that person's guidance, then an action verb (励む・学ぶ).
〜に基づいて needs a criterion such as a law or data. A coach is a person you train under, not a yardstick.
〜をもとに is for source material you create from. A coach is not material.
〜に沿って follows a plan or a manual. A person is not a plan.
tell: Training or working under a person (先生・監督・師匠) + an action verb: のもとで.

s: かつては「教育」という名（　　）、子どもへの体罰が当然のように行われていた。
en: In the past, physical punishment of children was carried out as a matter of course in the name of 'education'.
why: 〜の名のもとに: 'in the name of'. のもとに takes a condition or situation noun such as 名, 管理 or 了解.
〜をもとに is for source material you create from. A name is not material, and punishment creates nothing.
〜に沿って means following a plan or policy. 名 is not a plan you follow.
〜を通じて means 'via' a go-between or 'throughout' a period. A name is neither.
tell: Condition nouns (名・管理・了解) take のもとに: 〜の名のもとに = in the name of.

s: 彼は高校を卒業した後、有名な陶芸家（　　）十年間修業を積んだ。
en: After finishing high school, he trained for ten years under a famous potter.
why: Person + のもとで: train or study under that person. 修業を積む is the action.
〜をもとに is for source material you create from. A potter is a person, not material.
〜に沿って means following a plan or policy. A person is not a plan.
〜向けに means 'made for a target group'. He trained under the potter, not for him.
tell: Studying or training under a master: person + のもとで.

s: このプログラミングの入門書は、専門用語をできるだけ使わず、IT初心者（　　）書かれている。
en: This introductory programming book avoids jargon as far as possible and is written for IT beginners.
why: 〜向けに: deliberately made for a target group. Avoiding jargon shows the writer aimed the book at beginners.
〜をもとに names the source material a work is built from. Beginners are the readers, not the material.
〜にとって means 'from X's point of view' and is followed by an evaluation (大切だ・難しい). 書かれている is not one.
〜として means 'in the role of'. The book was not written in the role of a beginner.
cue: 専門用語をできるだけ使わず
tell: Written or made on purpose for a target group (書く・作る・開発する): noun + 向けに.

s: 当店では、小さなお子様（　　）、量を少なめにしたメニューもご用意しております。
en: We also offer a menu with smaller portions for young children.
why: 〜向けに: made for a target group. The smaller portions are designed for young children.
〜次第で means 'depending on X'. Nothing here varies with the children.
〜をめぐって is for a dispute between several sides. Nobody is arguing about children.
〜にかけては praises a skill where someone is the best. Children are not a skill.
tell: A product or service designed for a group of people: noun + 向け(に・の).

s: 台風が列島に（　　）、次第に風雨が強まり、波も高くなってきた。
en: As the typhoon approached the islands, the wind and rain gradually grew stronger and the waves rose higher.
why: 〜につれて: as one thing changes step by step, another changes with it. 次第に and 〜てきた show gradual change.
〜次第 (as soon as) attaches to the ます stem (近づき次第) and must lead into a plan or request, not a natural change.
〜上で means 'after doing X carefully, then Y'. A typhoon does not take deliberate steps.
〜たとたん marks one instant followed by a surprise. 次第に and 〜てきた show a slow change, so they clash.
tell: Change ↔ gradual change (次第に・〜てきた): dictionary form + につれて.

s: A「最近、ケーキをあまり食べなくなったね。」B「うん、年を取る（　　）、だんだん甘いものが苦手になってきたんだ。」
en: A: You don't eat much cake these days. B: No. As I've got older, I've gradually gone off sweet things.
why: 〜につれて: as X progresses, Y changes bit by bit (だんだん). It sits naturally in casual speech.
〜限り 'as long as' links two lasting states. It cannot lead into a change that has already happened (苦手になってきた).
〜次第で means 'depending on X' and attaches to a noun. 年を取る is a verb, and nothing depends on it.
〜一方で sets two different things side by side. Ageing and losing a sweet tooth move together; they are not a contrast.
tell: Gradual change on both sides (だんだん〜てきた): につれて. No will or plan after it.

s: 子どもが成長するにつれて、（　　）。
en: As our children grew up, we gradually spent less time talking together as a family.
c: 親子で話す時間は少しずつ減っていった
もっと広い家に引っ越そうと思っている
子どもは春に小学校に入学した
家族でもっと旅行に行きましょう
why: After 〜につれて comes a natural change that moves along with the first one: 少しずつ減っていった.
〜につれて cannot be followed by the speaker's will or plan (〜よう・〜たい・〜つもり).
Starting school is a single event, not a gradual change. 〜につれて links change to change.
〜につれて cannot be followed by an invitation or request (〜ましょう).
tell: After につれて: a natural, gradual change. No will (〜よう), no invitation (〜ましょう), no one-off event.

s: 新しい駅の開業（　　）、駅周辺の土地の値段が大きく上がった。
en: With the opening of the new station, land prices around it rose sharply.
why: 〜に伴って: a change seen as one whole (the opening) brings another change with it. Formal, and fits a news style.
〜につれて needs a gradual change before it (増える・進む). 開業 is a one-off event, not a gradual change.
〜次第で means 'depending on X'. The rise in prices did not depend on how the opening turned out.
〜に応じて means 'adjusting to something that varies'. An opening is not a variable.
tell: A one-off change (開業・移転・合併) bringing other changes: に伴って. につれて needs a gradual change.

s: 本社の移転（　　）、電話番号とファクス番号が下記のとおり変わります。
en: Due to the relocation of our head office, our telephone and fax numbers will change as follows.
why: 〜に伴い (formal に伴って): one change (the move) brings another with it. Standard wording on notices.
〜につれ links two gradual changes. A move is one event, and the numbers do not change little by little.
〜に応じ means 'adjusting to something that varies'. A move is not a variable.
〜にかけて marks a span from one point to another (春から夏にかけて). It does not mark a cause.
tell: On a notice: 移転・改装・変更 + に伴い + what changes.

s: この町では、人口の減少に伴って、（　　）。
en: In this town, primary schools are being merged as the population falls.
c: 小学校の統合が進められている
地域の行事にもっと参加しよう
古い寺や神社が多く残っている
町の人口は約二万人だ
why: 〜に伴って needs a change on both sides. A falling population brings another change: schools being merged.
This is a call to act (〜よう). 〜に伴って links two changes; it is not followed by the speaker's will.
Having many old temples is a fixed state, not a change brought about by the falling population.
A population figure is a fact, not a change. 〜に伴って needs something that changes.
tell: Change + に伴って + another change. A fixed fact or the speaker's will does not fit.

s: 入社試験に合格できるかどうかは、筆記試験と面接の（　　）。
en: Whether you pass the company's entrance exam depends on the results of the written test and the interview.
why: Noun + 次第だ: 'depends on X'. 〜かどうかは … 次第だ is the standard frame, and it ends the sentence.
〜次第で needs a clause after it (次第で決まる). The sentence ends at the blank.
〜に沿って must lead into an action that follows a plan. It cannot end a sentence, and results are not a plan.
〜をもとに must lead into a creation verb (作る). It cannot end the sentence.
tell: 〜かどうかは + noun + 次第だ: 'whether … depends on X'.

s: 明日の試合を行うかどうかは、朝の天気（　　）決めます。
en: We'll decide whether to hold tomorrow's match depending on the weather in the morning.
why: Noun + 次第で: the decision depends on the weather. 〜かどうか shows the outcome could go either way.
次第に is an adverb meaning 'gradually'. 'Decide gradually the weather' makes no sense.
〜につれて links two gradual changes. Deciding once in the morning is not a gradual change.
〜に限って means 'on that occasion of all times', usually a complaint. It does not mean 'depending on'.
tell: Noun + 次第で + 決める・変わる: 'depending on'. 次第に just means 'gradually'.

s: この薬の効き方は、その人の体質次第で、（　　）。
en: How well this medicine works depends on each person's constitution: it works well for some and hardly at all for others.
c: よく効く人もいれば、ほとんど効かない人もいる
だれにでも同じように効く
飲めば必ず三日で治る
毎食後に飲む必要がある
why: After 〜次第で comes a result that varies with X. 'Works for some, not for others' is exactly that variation.
'Works the same for everyone' denies any variation, so it contradicts 次第で.
'Always cures in three days' is a fixed result. 次第で says the result is not fixed.
How often to take it is an instruction, not a result that depends on the person's constitution.
tell: After 次第で: a result that changes with X (〜もいれば〜もいる). A fixed result contradicts it.

s: お客様の年齢や（　　）、最適な保険プランをご提案いたします。
en: We will suggest the best insurance plan for you according to your age and budget.
why: 〜に応じて: adjust to something that varies from person to person (年齢・予算). The plan changes to match.
〜にこたえて only takes expectations or requests (期待・要望). A budget is a variable, not a request.
〜をめぐって is for a dispute between several sides. Nobody is arguing over the budget.
〜にかけては praises a skill where someone is the best. A budget is not a skill.
tell: Adjust to something that varies (年齢・予算・体力): に応じて. にこたえて is for expectations.

s: この料理教室では、参加者の経験（　　）、初級・中級・上級の三つのクラスを用意している。
en: This cooking school offers three classes, beginner, intermediate and advanced, to match participants' experience.
why: 〜に応じて: match something that varies. Experience differs from person to person, so there are three levels.
〜にこたえて only takes expectations or requests (期待・要望). Experience is neither.
〜をめぐって is for a dispute between several sides. Nobody is arguing.
〜にかけては praises someone who is the best at a skill. Offering three classes is not praise.
tell: Several options to match something that varies (経験・年齢・予算): に応じて.

s: 学生時代のアルバムを（　　）、仲間たちと過ごした懐かしい日々を思い出す。
en: Whenever I look at my old school album, I remember the happy days I spent with my friends.
why: Dictionary form + につけて: every time I do X, a feeling or memory rises up. 思い出す is a movement of the heart.
〜一方だ means 'keeps on ~ing' and ends a sentence. It cannot link to a second clause.
〜最中に needs the ている form or 名の (見ている最中に), and it is for an interruption, not a memory.
〜ばかりに means 'just because of X, something bad happened'. Remembering happy days is not a bad result.
tell: Every time I do X + a feeling (思い出す・心配になる): dictionary form + につけて.

s: 隣に住むおばあさんは、何か（　　）うちの子どもたちのことを気にかけてくれる。
en: The old lady next door looks out for our children at every opportunity.
why: 何かにつけて is a set phrase: 'at every opportunity'. In this phrase, what follows need not be a feeling.
〜につれて links two gradual changes and follows a change verb. 何か is not a change.
〜にかけては praises a skill where someone is the best. 何か is not a skill.
〜に限って picks out one special case, often in a complaint. 何かに限って is not a phrase.
tell: 何か + につけて = at every opportunity. A fixed phrase worth learning whole.

s: 最近の物価高のニュースを見るにつけ、（　　）。
en: Every time I see news about rising prices these days, I start to worry about how I will live in old age.
c: 老後の生活が心配になる
すぐに節約を始めることにしている
毎日家計簿をつけている
物価は去年より五パーセント上がった
why: After 〜につけ comes a feeling that rises by itself each time (心配になる・思い出す). Worry about old age is exactly that.
Deciding to start saving is a deliberate rule you follow. 〜につけ is followed by a feeling, not a decision.
Keeping a household account book every day is a habit. It does not rise each time you see the news.
'Prices rose 5% on last year' is a plain fact. It is not a feeling that comes each time.
tell: After につけ: a feeling or memory (思い出す・心配になる). Not an action, not a plain fact.

s: 引っ越しの前の週は、荷造り（　　）役所での手続きやらで、ゆっくり眠る暇もなかった。
en: The week before the move, what with packing and paperwork at the city office, I didn't even have time to sleep properly.
why: 〜やら〜やら(で): a messy pile of jobs that wore you out. The second やら in 手続きやらで completes the pair.
〜というか〜というか gives two labels for ONE impression and needs というか twice. Packing and paperwork are separate jobs.
〜にせよ〜にせよ means 'whether X or Y' and leads to a judgement. It does not pair with やら, and nothing is being weighed.
〜といった wraps up examples before a category noun. Packing is not an example of paperwork at the city office.
tell: A pile of chores + 大変だった・暇もなかった: 〜やら〜やらで.

s: 社長から急に表彰されて、（　　）、どんな顔をすればいいのかわからなかった。
en: When the company president suddenly gave me an award, I felt so pleased and so embarrassed that I didn't know what face to make.
c: うれしいやら照れくさいやら
うれしいにせよ照れくさいにせよ
うれしいだの照れくさいだの
うれしいばかりか照れくさくて
why: 〜やら〜やら lists mixed feelings that hit you all at once and leave you flustered.
〜にせよ〜にせよ means 'whether X or Y' and leads to a judgement or advice. Here both feelings happened together.
〜だの〜だの lists things someone keeps saying, with irritation. Nobody is complaining here.
〜ばかりか adds a bigger step in the same direction. Embarrassment is not a bigger kind of happiness.
cue: どんな顔をすればいいのかわからなかった
tell: Mixed feelings all at once that leave you flustered: 〜やら〜やら.

s: 彼の遠慮のない発言は、率直（　　）無礼というか、聞く人によって受け止め方が大きく分かれる。
en: His blunt remarks are frank, or perhaps rude: people take them very differently depending on who is listening.
why: 〜というか〜というか: two labels for one thing, because neither fits perfectly. The second というか completes the pair.
〜やら〜やら lists separate things that pile up. It does not pair with というか, and his remarks are one thing.
〜にせよ〜にせよ means 'whether X or Y' and needs the same form twice. It does not pair with というか.
〜といった wraps up examples before a category noun. 無礼 is not a category that 率直 belongs to.
tell: One thing, two possible labels, and you can't decide: 〜というか〜というか.

s: うちの祖父は、（　　）、九十歳を過ぎても一人で山に登ろうとする。
en: My grandfather is full of energy, or maybe just reckless: even past ninety, he still tries to climb mountains on his own.
c: 元気というか無茶というか
元気にせよ無茶にせよ
why: 〜というか〜というか: two labels for one person's behaviour, because the speaker can't decide which fits.
〜やら〜やら lists several separate things that pile up and overwhelm you. Here one habit is being described.
〜にせよ〜にせよ means 'whether X or Y' and leads to a judgement or advice. The sentence just describes him.
〜だの〜だの lists things someone keeps saying, with irritation. Nobody is being quoted here.
cue: 一人で山に登ろうとする
tell: One person or event, two labels that half fit: 〜というか〜というか.

s: 提案に（　　）、会議ではその理由をはっきり説明するべきだ。
en: Whether you are for or against the proposal, you should explain your reasons clearly at the meeting.
c: 賛成するにせよ反対するにせよ
賛成するやら反対するやら
賛成するというか反対するというか
賛成するばかりか反対するばかりか
why: 〜にせよ〜にせよ: whichever of two opposite options you take, the same rule holds. べきだ is that judgement.
〜やら〜やら lists a messy pile of things that happened. It does not set up two options.
〜というか〜というか gives two labels for one impression. For and against are opposite choices, not two labels.
〜ばかりか adds a bigger step to a first point. It never pairs with itself, and you cannot be both for and against.
tell: Two opposite options + a rule for both (べきだ・必要がある): 〜にせよ〜にせよ.

s: 来月の研修会について、参加するにしても参加しないにしても、（　　）。
en: About next month's training session: whether or not you attend, please be sure to reply by the end of this week.
c: 今週中に必ず返事をしてください
参加者は全部で三十人だった
結局、参加することにした
どちらにするかまだ迷っている
why: After 〜にしても〜にしても comes something that holds either way: a judgement, advice or a request.
A past headcount is a plain fact. It is not something that applies whichever option you choose.
Deciding to attend picks one option. 〜にしても〜にしても needs a point that holds for both.
The pair has already set aside which option you pick. Saying you are still undecided goes back on that.
cue: 参加するにしても参加しないにしても
tell: After 〜にしても〜にしても: a point valid for both options, often advice or a request.

s: この地域では、りんごやぶどう（　　）果物の栽培が盛んだ。
en: Fruit such as apples and grapes is widely grown in this region.
why: 〜といった + noun: wraps up examples (りんご, ぶどう) into a category (果物). Often with や before it.
〜やら needs a pair (〜やら〜やら) and a sense of chaos. It cannot link examples to a category noun.
〜というか gives two labels for one impression and comes in a pair. It cannot sit before a noun.
〜にせよ means 'whether X or Y' and comes in a pair. It cannot link examples to a category.
tell: Examples (A や B) + といった + a category noun.

s: 「おもてなし」という言葉は、相手の気持ちを考えて行動する（　　）意味で使われることが多い。
en: The word 'omotenashi' is often used to mean something like acting with the other person's feelings in mind.
why: 〜といった + noun can also give one rough example of what a word means: 〜といった意味 = 'a meaning like ~'.
〜というか gives two uncertain labels and comes in a pair. It cannot sit before a noun like 意味.
〜やら lists chaotic things in a pair. It cannot describe a noun like 意味.
〜にしても means 'whether' or 'even if' and leads into a judgement. It cannot describe 意味.
tell: Roughly what a word means: 〜といった意味. といった must be followed by a noun.
